summary: Two standoffs hardened this week and neither moved. On the delivery side, Vivek did not send a single message in the entire window. Lauryn chased him three times on Sep 2 ('Hey, @fonta' / 'Any updates???' / 'We still in review ??'), again on Sep 3 ('???'), and Mayson escalated internally ('@fonta ^^', Sep 3) - nothing came back. His last words on this account remain 'Still in review' (Aug 26), so the Facebook 'not recommended' flag she first raised on 2025-09-27 is now 342 days old and 9 days without any status at all. Last week's state file predicted exactly this and said escalate off Vivek if the answer was still 'in review' on Sep 4; the answer is now worse than 'in review', it is silence. On the money side, Stephski chased on Aug 30 ('please let us know when you can get your last 2 invoices paid'), then issued the Aug 15-31 invoice on Sep 1 with a 7-day term and an explicit warning - 'Also ask that you settle this invoice within 7 days to avoid us pausing work'. Lauryn did not dispute a cent but paid nothing, and for the second week running she pointed the reason at us: 'I'm well aware of payments being team has had a very slow month things aren't dropping quick!' and 'The monies are on hold !' (Sep 2). She did volunteer a screenshot of her pending OF balance on Sep 3 - the first proof she has ever offered - and said 'Watching pending balance now just sitting soon as it opens it's coming your way'. Three billing periods are now unsettled and this is the sixth consecutive period carrying a balance. Meanwhile the only new ALTR asks of the week were for MORE unpaid work from her: Mayson demanded a fresh content Drive with '7 reels a week so 30 in total per month' (Aug 30) for what he called a 'separate instagram account', which she did not understand and had to re-ask about twice, and Mica sent a posting-consistency nudge the next night. Michelle's DMCA leak update (Sep 1) was, for the sixth straight week, the only thing ALTR actually delivered. Derrek has not posted since Aug 13 (22 days) and Lauryn has stopped asking for him. The 'Lauryn chat team' vendor group has now been silent for 86 days.

health.rationale: Down 8 from 40. Volume recovered (32 messages vs 12) but every additional message made the position worse. (1) Vivek went from two one-liners to zero: four client chases and one internal tag across Sep 2-3 got no reply at all, so the 342-day Facebook complaint has gone a full week with no status. Communication has now failed in three consecutive weekly windows and this is the worst of the three. (2) The payment problem escalated on both sides. Stephski had to write 'we are multiple invoices unpaid' language for a second week, then attached an explicit service-pause threat to the Sep 1 invoice; Lauryn repeated and hardened the ALTR-blame framing she introduced on Aug 27, moving from 'only moving off what's being funneled' to naming us directly - 'team has had a very slow month things aren't dropping quick'. Three periods are now unsettled, the sixth consecutive period carrying a balance, and nothing was paid in seven days. (3) The only new work ALTR proposed was 30 reels a month FROM her, for a purpose she asked about three times and never got a clear answer to, while her Facebook page is still throttled and she has already said she will not post 'in this state of page'. Holding the score off the 20s: she is still warm and has never disputed an amount, she proactively sent a screenshot of her pending balance on Sep 3, Stephski invoiced on time and offered a partial-payment path, and Michelle's DMCA update landed for the sixth straight week.

suggestions: Take the Meta appeal off Vivek this week. He has had 28 days, 19 of them with full account access, and produced no dated plan and no reply to five direct prompts across Sep 2-3. Either name a new owner with a written plan and a date, or tell her honestly that the flag may not clear and pivot the strategy to Instagram and TikTok. Nine more days of silence will cost more than an unwelcome answer.

Answer her one open question before anything else: she asked 'We still in review ??' on Sep 2 and '???' on Sep 3 and got nothing. Even 'no change, here is what we try next and by when' resets the relationship at zero cost.

Do not send another invoice or another chase until we can point at delivered work. She has now said twice that she pays out of what the page produces. Chasing does not fix a value objection - delivering does. Reverse the order: get someone visibly working the page, tell her who they are, then bill.

Get a named chat team introduced in the thread this week. The last vendor message was 2026-06-10 and the replacement Mayson promised the same day has never appeared. 86 days of silence is the root cause of both the revenue complaint and the payment stall.

Restate the Aug 15-31 invoice IN THE CHAT with the total, the due date and an itemised $1,852.15 carryover line, and confirm which rail to use. The Aug 15 account number and Zelle details have still never had a payment attempted on them in 20 days, and the last two cycles were both delayed by ALTR-side rail failures - do not discover a broken rail during a live collections conversation.

Accept the increment offer explicitly and put a floor under it. She said 'as it drops you will receive invoices in increments' and sent a screenshot of the pending balance. Agree a first tranche and a specific date rather than leaving it open-ended for a seventh period.

Pull the 30-reels-a-month request until the page is unblocked and the bill is settled, or re-brief it properly. Asking a client for 30 pieces of unpaid content a month, for a 'separate instagram account' she has never been briefed on, while three invoices are unpaid and her page is throttled, reads as tone-deaf. If the plan is real, send her one paragraph explaining what the account is, who runs it and what she gets from it.

Rotate the two exposed Facebook passwords, delete the credential and 2FA messages from the thread, and issue a one-line written policy that credentials never go in the group chat. 28 days open, four weeks logged, zero action - and her management has already told her not to share passwords.
